title: The first minute
hook: what you do in your first waking minute shapes the day
tomorrow: a full moon, a hall of monks, and the Buddha teaches… breathing?

segments.voice: Yesterday, one notebook: your rule kept in one place, where you can find it again. Now the notebook needs a first page, and the day needs a first thing. The daily practice starts at the very top.

The alarm goes off, and before your feet find the floor, the phone has already handed you the day: a group chat, the news, somebody's vacation. Mark's Gospel tells about a morning that went another way. The evening before, in the town of Capernaum, the whole city gathered at one door, bringing the sick to Jesus as the sun went down. Late that night the house finally goes quiet. And in the dark, the man everyone wants is gone.
screen: `THE PHONE HANDS YOU THE DAY.` → `A WHOLE CITY AT ONE DOOR.` → `IN THE DARK, HE'S GONE.`

segments.voice: Mark says it in one line: "And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed." Simon and the others go looking. When they find him, their first words land like a buzzing phone: "All men seek for thee." Everyone's waiting. Come back. And Jesus doesn't go back. He says, let us go on to the next towns, because that is what I came out for. The hour alone came first, and out of it came his answer to the crowd. Here is the teaching under the story. In Mark, Jesus slips away alone to pray at turning points: here, again after he feeds the crowd, and in Gethsemane. Some Christians have taken that solitary place as a pattern for an ordinary day: the first of the day is given to God before anyone else can claim it. They call it a morning watch or a quiet time, a few minutes of prayer or scripture before the coffee and the crowd. Notice what the prayer did and didn't do. The crowd didn't vanish. He met them knowing what he was for. On your own path you can borrow this with the tag left on: Mark's morning, a first minute given away on purpose, before the day starts giving orders.
screen: `RISING UP A GREAT WHILE BEFORE DAY.` · `ALL MEN SEEK FOR THEE.` · `ON TO THE NEXT TOWNS.` · `THE FIRST OF THE DAY, GIVEN FIRST.` · then, large: `THE FIRST MINUTE.`

segments.voice: Open yesterday's notebook and write tomorrow's first minute by hand: where your feet land, what your hands do, what you'll say or think before the phone. If you pray, that minute might hold a line of prayer, the way Jesus kept the dark hour; if not, it might hold a window, a breath, a glass of water. Keep it to one minute you could really keep.
The first minute: the opening of the day, given on purpose before anything else claims it. In Mark, a solitary place, a great while before day.
Pocket this one: the first minute, and in Mark the prayer came before the crowd. The daily practice has begun.

howItsDone: Some Christians keep a morning watch or quiet time, a few minutes of prayer or scripture before the day begins, following Gospel pictures like Mark's of Jesus praying alone before dawn.

Mark's Gospel.meaning: one of the four Gospels telling the life of Jesus

Capernaum.meaning: a lakeside town in Galilee where Jesus stayed and healed

Gethsemane.meaning: the garden where Jesus prayed alone the night of his arrest

quiet time.meaning: a few minutes of prayer or reading some Christians keep each morning
